risikabel.explanation: "Risikabel" means "risky". It is built from "en risiko" (a risk). Do not use it for something that can hurt you. To say a dog is dangerous, use "farlig" (dangerous): "en farlig hund" (a dangerous dog).

ro.explanation: "Ro" means "calm / peace and quiet". To say you find peace, use "at finde ro" (to find peace): "Jeg finder ro i skoven" (I find peace in the forest). To tell someone to relax, say "Slap af" (Relax).

robust.explanation: "Robust" means "robust". When you describe a bag that does not break easily, say: "en robust rygsæk" (a sturdy backpack). When you describe a person who does not get sick or upset easily, say: "Hun er robust" (She is tough).

rock.explanation: "Rock" means "rock" as in music. To name a show of this music, put "rock" in front of "koncert" (concert): "en rockkoncert" (a rock concert). For the stone, say "en sten" (a stone): "Der ligger en sten på vejen" (There is a stone in the road).

rodet.explanation: "Rodet" means "messy". It is about things lying around, not dirt. To say a room is messy but clean, say: "Rummet er rodet, men ikke snavset" (The room is messy, but not dirty).

rolig.explanation: "Rolig" means "calm". To tell someone to stay calm, say: "Vær rolig" (Stay calm). To describe a quiet street, say: "en rolig gade" (a quiet street). To say how to speak, use the form "roligt": "Tal roligt" (Speak calmly).

romantik.explanation: "Romantik" means "romance". To say a chore has no romance, say: "Der er ikke meget romantik i at vaske op" (There is not much romance in doing the dishes).

romantisk.explanation: "Romantisk" means "romantic". It is built on "romantik" (romance). To describe a dinner for two, say: "en romantisk middag" (a romantic dinner).

roning.explanation: "Roning" means "rowing". It is the noun for "at ro" (to row), and a person who does it is "en roer" (a rower).

ros.explanation: "Ros" means "praise". To say someone deserves praise, say: "Hun fortjener ros" (She deserves praise).

rug.explanation: "En rug" means "rye". To name the bread made from it, add "brød" (bread): "rugbrød" (rye bread).

rugbrød.explanation: "Rugbrød" means "rye bread". It is built from "rug" (rye) and "brød" (bread). In Denmark, "smørrebrød" (open sandwiches) are traditionally made on a slice of it.

rummelig.explanation: "Rummelig" means "spacious". It is built on "et rum" (a room, a space). To describe a bag with a lot of space, say: "en rummelig taske" (a spacious bag).

rund.explanation: "Rund" means "round". To say a number is round, say: "Hundrede er et rundt tal" (One hundred is a round number).

rundt om hjørnet.explanation: "Rundt om hjørnet" means "around the corner". To say a place is close, say: "Posthuset ligger rundt om hjørnet" (The post office is around the corner). To say a date is coming soon, say: "Julen er lige rundt om hjørnet" (Christmas is just around the corner).

rusland.explanation: "Rusland" means "Russia". Use "i" (in) for being there and "til" (to) for going there: "Jeg bor i Rusland" (I live in Russia), "Jeg rejser til Rusland" (I am traveling to Russia).

russisk.explanation: "Russisk" means "Russian". To ask for a word in the language, use "på" (in): "Hvad hedder det på russisk?" (What is it called in Russian?). Danish does not start the word with "R" as English does, and the country is "Rusland" (Russia).

ryddelig.explanation: "Ryddelig" means "tidy". It comes from the verb "at rydde" (to clear). To say you tidy up, use "at rydde op" (to tidy up): "Jeg rydder op i stuen" (I am tidying up the living room).

rynket.explanation: "Rynket" means "wrinkled". It comes from "at rynke" (to wrinkle). To say you frown, use "at rynke panden" (literally, to wrinkle the forehead).

rystende.explanation: "Rystende" means "shocking". It comes from "at ryste" (to shake). When you describe hands that tremble, it means "trembling": "rystende hænder" (trembling hands).

rystet.explanation: "Rystet" means "shaken". It comes from "at ryste" (to shake). To say news has upset you, use "over" (about): "Vi er alle rystede over nyheden" (We are all shaken by the news).

rå.explanation: "Rå" means "raw". When you describe food that is not cooked, say: "rå fisk" (raw fish). When you describe harsh words, it means "crude": "et råt sprog" (crude language).

rædselsslagen.explanation: "Rædselsslagen" means "terrified". It is built from "en rædsel" (a horror) and "slagen" (struck), so it is literally "struck by horror". It is much stronger than "bange" (afraid): "Jeg er bange for edderkopper" (I am afraid of spiders).

rød.explanation: "Rød" means "red". It is the first part of words such as "rødvin" (red wine) and "rødbede" (beetroot).

rødgrød.explanation: "En rødgrød" means "red berry pudding". It is built from "rød" (red) and "grød" (porridge). Despite the ending "grød", it is a pudding, not a porridge.
